documents.title: Tram Line Extension Gets Green Light
documents.text: MARBURY (October 2) - The Marbury City Council voted 7 to 2 on Tuesday to extend the Line 3 tram by six kilometers to the Eastfield business district. [A] The extension, which will include eight new stops, is expected to cost $310 million and will open in 2029. [B] Supporters say the line will relieve congestion on Highway 12, where commuters currently spend an average of 40 minutes each way. [C] Opponents argue that the money would be better spent on bus service, which carries more passengers at lower cost. [D] The project will be funded by a federal transit grant covering 60 percent of the cost, with the city and the regional transit authority splitting the remainder. A final environmental review is scheduled for next spring.

questions.prompt: What did the council decide on Tuesday?
choices: To close a highway near the city
To lengthen an existing tram line
To buy new buses for the city
questions.explanation: The council voted to extend the Line 3 tram.

questions.explanation: A federal grant covers 60 percent; the rest is split between the city and the transit authority.

questions.explanation: Relieving congestion means reducing it.

questions.prompt: In which position marked [A], [B], [C] or [D] does the following sentence best belong? "The vote followed three hours of public comment."
questions.explanation: It directly follows the first sentence, which reports the council's vote.

documents.title: ParkEasy: Frequently Asked Questions
documents.text:
Q: How do I pay?
A: Enter your license plate and the zone number in the app, then choose how long you want to park. Payment is charged to your saved card.

Q: Can I extend my parking remotely?
A: Yes, as long as the zone's maximum stay (shown in the app) has not been reached. A reminder is sent 10 minutes before your time ends.

Q: What if I park for less time than I paid for?
A: The app does not offer refunds for unused time.

Q: Is there a fee?
A: A service fee of $0.35 per transaction applies.

Q: Which cities are supported?
A: Currently Marbury, Eastfield, and Dunlap. Riverton will be added in January.

documents.title: Lakeside Elementary School: Weather Policy
documents.text: When severe weather forces the school to close or delay opening, parents will be notified by 6:30 a.m. through three channels: a text message, the school website, and local radio station WKLR (95.3 FM). In the case of a two-hour delay, buses will run two hours later than usual, and breakfast will not be served. Morning kindergarten will be canceled on delay days. If the school closes early because of a storm during the day, buses will leave at 12:30 p.m., and parents who prefer to pick up their children should sign them out at the front office. Please make sure the office has your current phone number. Make-up days are added to the end of the school year.

documents.title: Packaging contract renewal
documents.text:
To: Hector Salinas, Bright Pack
From: Marguerite Boyle, Atlas Freight
Date: September 9

Dear Hector Salinas,
Our current contract for corrugated boxes expires on October 31. We have been satisfied with the quality, but our costs have risen, and we received a competitive quote from another supplier at $0.92 per box, compared with your current price of $1.05. We would prefer to continue with Bright Pack if you can come close to that price. Our annual volume is approximately 240,000 boxes. We would also like to discuss delivery terms. We currently receive shipments monthly, but more frequent deliveries would help us reduce storage costs.
Marguerite Boyle

documents.title: Re: Packaging contract renewal
documents.text:
To: Marguerite Boyle
From: Hector Salinas
Date: September 12

Dear Marguerite Boyle,
Thank you for letting us know. We value Atlas Freight's business. I can offer $0.96 per box for a two-year contract, provided that the annual volume stays above 200,000 boxes. For a one-year contract, our price would be $1.00. Deliveries every two weeks are possible at no extra charge; weekly deliveries would carry a $60 fee per shipment. Please let me know by September 20, as these prices are guaranteed only until then.
Hector Salinas

TO: Third-floor staff

SUBJECT: Renovation of the third floor

The third floor will be renovated from November 18 to December 13. During this period, affected employees will relocate temporarily to the first-floor conference area or work from home. New carpet, lighting, and workstations will be installed, and the break room will be enlarged. Please clear personal items from your desks by Friday, November 15. documents.title: Not worth the price
documents.text:
Ultra-Glide Office Chair: 2 stars out of 5
Posted by Martin W., verified purchase

I bought this chair for my home office three months ago. The cushion is comfortable at first, but after about six weeks the seat began to flatten, and the left armrest became loose. The assembly instructions were confusing. It took me nearly two hours, and one screw was missing. On the positive side, the wheels roll smoothly and the chair looks stylish. I contacted customer support twice and received no reply. I would advise buyers to look elsewhere.

documents.text:
To: Martin W.
From: Customer Experience Team, Ultra-Glide Furniture

Dear Martin,
We are sorry that your chair did not meet your expectations, and we apologize for the lack of response from our support team, which was short-staffed last month. Our chairs are covered by a two-year warranty, and the problems you describe qualify for a free replacement. Please reply with your order number and a photo of the loose armrest, and we will ship a new chair within five business days, along with a missing-parts kit and a revised assembly guide. We would be grateful if you would update your review after receiving the replacement.
Customer Experience Team
